Jon McNeill is the former President of Tesla and the co-founder and CEO of DVx Ventures. He is also the author of the book, The Algorithm.

Elon Musk believes speed creates a competitive advantage, whether it’s speed of decision, speed of cash, or speed of response. But what does that look like day to day, and how do you build a company around it?

Jon spent years inside Elon’s companies, and he explains how they work. We talk about what happens when you skip the chain of command, why bad news can’t wait, and why Elon wanted problems explained in three sentences.

We also get into the five-step algorithm Jon uses to simplify problems, why Elon treats a company like a garden full of weeds, and how Tesla grew with zero marketing budget.

Tiny Lessons

Speed, Action, and Decisions

  • “Speed of all types — speed of decision-making, speed of cash through the business, speed of response time — creates competitive advantage, because your competitors are probably moving slower.”
  • Action creates information. So waiting until you feel ready just puts you behind on the learning curve.
  • Start every decision by getting everyone to agree on what success looks like, then work backward from there.
  • “Your no list should be much bigger than your yes list.”
  • Look for bets where the upside is much bigger than the downside, and walk away from anything that can wipe you out unless you can remove that downside first.

Communication and Culture

  • “Don’t sit on bad news. Give me bad news as fast as you know about it.”
  • “Go straight across the organization. If you need an answer, go to the person who has that answer. Don’t go through their boss or their boss’s boss; go directly to them, because that’s going to help with speed of decision-making.”
  • If you have to deliver hard feedback, make sure the other person knows you respect them and want to help them fix it, rather than leaving them hanging.
  • Keep postmortems strictly clinical and focused on facts, because the moment you make a mistake personal, people get defensive and you lose the truth.
  • Slides tend to mask problems, so look at the actual product and touch it yourself whenever you can.

Product and Strategy

  • “The definition of a great product is that you don’t need a sales force. It sells itself.”
  • Simplicity is what makes a product great. “People tend to like and appreciate simplicity and pay for simplicity.”
  • “Never compete on price if you can avoid it, because the moment you do, you turn your business into a commodity and your margins collapse.”

The Algorithm

“The Algorithm was designed to supercharge speed, efficiency, innovation, and growth.”

  1. Question every requirement
  2. Delete every possible step
  3. Simplify and optimize
  4. Accelerate cycle time
  5. Automate last.

Fire Yourself

  • Ask yourself what your successor would do if you were fired tomorrow, and then do those things.
  • You can’t see the system you are standing inside, so you have to step outside your role to spot the fixes.

Hiring and Leadership

  • “You got to lead with your own authentic style, not somebody else’s. And when you start mimicking somebody’s style, like the people mimicking Jobs, it doesn’t really work well because people see it’s inauthentic, and it doesn’t really work for who you are.”
  • Separate the paper pushers from the doers. When you interview someone, dig into the details of how they solved a problem. “Tell me how you did that. Tell me how you broke this problem down. Tell me what the solution was. Tell me what your role in that solution was.”
  • “History is changed by unreasonable men.”
  • “You want to work for these people that just have an unreasonable view of the world because they bring out the best in [you].”

Mentors

  • You need two kinds of mentors at all times: vertical mentors who have already seen the movie, and horizontal mentors who are fighting the same battles you are right now.
  • A peer looking at your problem from the side will often see what you miss when you are staring at it head-on.
  • “When you become a really good leader, one of the signs of that is you’ve become a very good teacher.”
